title: Exploring Mixtures and their Separation: Chapter Introduction
subject: Chemistry
objective: Muddy water settles but milk never does: particle size decides how a mixture behaves. Solutions, colloids and suspensions, and the ways to separate them.

fill.q: A mixture whose particles are too small to see and never settle is a ____.
A mixture whose particles are large and settle on standing is a ____.
Milk is an example of a ____.
Scattering of a light beam by colloid particles is called the ____ effect.
Iron filings can be separated from sand using a ____.

tf.explain: It contains nitrogen, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide and more.

tf.q: A suspension's particles pass through filter paper.
tf.explain: They are large enough to be trapped by filter paper.

tf.q: A light beam is visible when passed through a true solution.
tf.explain: Solution particles are too small to scatter light.

tf.q: Colloid particles settle down on standing.

ar.r: Milk is a colloid whose particles scatter light.

ar.a: Muddy water becomes clear on standing.
ar.r: Suspension particles are pulled down by gravity.

mcq.q: The size of colloid particles is about:
Coloured components of an ink are best separated by:
mcq.explain: Components travel at different speeds on paper.

mcq.q: Salt can be recovered from sea water by:
mcq.explain: The water evaporates and the salt is left.

short.q: Explain why mud settles but milk does not.
short.solution: Mud particles are large (a suspension), so gravity pulls them down. Milk's particles are mid-size (a colloid); they stay dispersed and only scatter light.

short.q: Name a method to separate each: sand + water, salt + water, iron + sand, inks.
short.solution: Sand + water: filtration; salt + water: evaporation; iron + sand: magnet; inks: chromatography.

match.explain: Each mixture matches its type or separation method.
